meta_description: Safay is a free, open-source two-factor authenticator. It keeps your TOTP codes in an encrypted vault on your own device and backs it up to storage you choose, with no account and no server.
privacy_meta_description: Safay collects no data. How the app, its backups to Google Drive, Dropbox and OneDrive, and this website handle information.
hero_title_full: A secure, simple, modern, and private authenticator.
hero_title_sub: No account, no server. Your codes stay encrypted on your device.
hero_cta_note: Free and open source · macOS 14 or later · Apple silicon
shot_main_alt: The Safay main window with eight sample accounts shown as cards, each with a six-digit code and a countdown ring. The left half is in light appearance, the right half in dark.
feat_1_text: Scan with the camera, select a QR code anywhere on screen, drop an image, paste an otpauth link, or type the key by hand.
feat_2_text: Import Google Authenticator migration codes and backups from Aegis, 2FAS, Ente Auth, Proton Authenticator and Bitwarden, or a CSV export from Apple Passwords.
feat_3_text: Search by service or account, sort accounts into categories (one account can be in several), drag to reorder, and switch between cards and a list.
feat_4_text: The vault locks after idle time and whenever the computer sleeps or its screen locks. Repeated wrong passwords add a delay.
feat_5_text: RFC 6238 TOTP with SHA-1, SHA-256 or SHA-512, 6 or 8 digits, 30 or 60 seconds, plus Steam Guard and Battle.net. One click copies a code.
feat_6_text: If two devices change the vault at once, review the differences and keep either copy or merge both. A damaged vault rolls back to the last good copy.
menubar_body: Open the panel from the menu bar or system tray, type a few letters, and click to copy a code. Global shortcuts open the panel or the main window, or let you select a QR code on screen to add an account.
shortcut_scan: Select a QR code on screen
shortcut_note: Shortcuts as on macOS; change them in Settings.
menubar_launchers: Alfred, Raycast and Tinycast can search your accounts too.
menubar_alt: The Safay quick panel open below its icon in a menu bar, listing sample accounts with their codes.
security_title: Encrypted on your device, and everywhere it goes.
security_intro: Safay is built on standard, well-studied cryptography, and its full security model is published with the source code.
sec_1_text: Accounts, secrets and categories live in a single encrypted vault on your device. Plaintext exists only in memory while the vault is unlocked, and there is no Safay server that could ever receive it.
sec_2_text: AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption, with the key derived from your master password by Argon2id (RFC 9106, 64 MiB, 3 passes). Every vault has its own random salt, and a tampered file is rejected.
sec_3_text: Unlock with a fingerprint where the device has a secure chip for it: with Touch ID, the vault key stays wrapped by the Secure Enclave. The master password is never stored, and Safay never sees your fingerprint.
sec_4_text: An export file is encrypted with a password of its own, in the same format as the vault. Nothing is imported until the file passes authentication.
sec_5_text: A backup location only ever holds the encrypted vault, a device name and a time. The storage provider can't read your accounts, and a backup opens only with your master password.
sync_title: Back up to the storage you already trust
sync_body: Turn on backup and Safay keeps an encrypted copy of your vault in one place you choose, and syncs changes from your other devices through it.
sync_folder_note: On Dropbox, OneDrive and Google Drive, the backup is kept in Safay's own folder: Apps › Safay, or a Safay folder in My Drive.
dl_title: Free, with no account to create.
dl_body: Safay is open source under the MIT license, with no ads, in-app purchases or tracking. The app is signed and notarized, and updates itself once you agree.
dl_body_android: Safay is open source under the MIT license, with no ads, in-app purchases or tracking. The APK is signed by Safay; to update, install a newer one over it.

privacy_summary: Safay collects no personal data. It has no account system, no analytics and no server of its own, so there is nothing for us to sell, share or lose.
privacy_app_vault: Your accounts stay on your device. Accounts (with their websites and icons), secrets and categories are stored in a vault encrypted with AES-256-GCM, using a key derived from your master password with Argon2id. The master password is never stored.
privacy_app_biometrics: Biometric unlock is handled by the system. Touch ID only releases vault key material protected by the Secure Enclave. Safay never sees your fingerprint.
privacy_app_camera: Scanning happens on the device. Camera images, dropped images and screen selections used to read QR codes are processed locally and never uploaded.
privacy_app_icons: Site icons come from the site itself. When you add an account or change its website, Safay downloads that website's icon directly from it, so the site sees one request from your IP address. No other service is involved. The website and icon are stored in your encrypted vault. You can turn this off in Settings.
privacy_app_updates: Update checks. After you agree, Safay checks GitHub once a day for a new version and downloads it from there. The request carries nothing about you or your vault. You can turn it off in Settings.
privacy_app_none: Safay has no telemetry, crash reporting, advertising or tracking of any kind.
privacy_backup_where: Backups go only where you choose. Backup is off until you turn it on. You then pick one location: iCloud, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive, Nextcloud, a WebDAV server, or a folder. The connection goes directly from your device to that service. There is no Safay server in between, and we never see it.
privacy_backup_what: Only ciphertext leaves the device. Safay uploads two files: the encrypted vault, and a small metadata file with the device's name and the time of the backup. Without your master password, neither the storage provider nor anyone else can read your accounts.
privacy_backup_icloud: iCloud. Safay uses your private iCloud database through the system. It reads no other iCloud data, and remembers only an opaque account identifier so that it stops syncing if the device switches to another Apple Account.
privacy_cloud_intro: When you choose one of these services, you sign in on the provider's own page and allow Safay to keep its backup there. This is what Safay does with that permission:
privacy_cloud_access: What Safay can access. Only its own app folder: Apps › Safay on Dropbox and OneDrive, and a folder named Safay in My Drive on Google Drive, where the permission covers only the files Safay itself creates. Safay reads and writes its two backup files there and nothing else. It can't see the rest of your files.
privacy_cloud_account: Account information. Safay reads the name or email address of the account you signed in with, only to show you which account the backup uses. It is stored on your device.
privacy_cloud_tokens: Sign-in tokens. The tokens the provider issues are stored on your device in the system keychain. They are sent only to that provider, to read and write the backup.
privacy_cloud_share: No sharing. Safay sends none of this to us or to any third party, because it has no server. It is never used for advertising, analytics or anything other than keeping your backup.
privacy_cloud_remove: Removing access. Turning off backup in Safay revokes the sign-in where the provider supports it and deletes the stored tokens. You can also remove Safay from the provider's list of connected apps at any time. The backup files stay in your storage until you delete them.
privacy_cloud_google: Safay's use of information received from Google APIs adheres to the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements. Each provider's own privacy policy applies to what you store with it.
privacy_site_body: safay.gicek.com is a static website hosted on Cloudflare. It sets no cookies and loads no analytics, third-party scripts or third-party fonts. Your language choice is remembered in your browser's local storage only. Cloudflare processes requests, including your IP address, to deliver and protect the site, as described in Cloudflare's privacy policy. Downloads are served by GitHub under its own privacy policy.
privacy_children_body: Safay doesn't collect data from anyone, including children.
privacy_changes_body: If this policy changes, the new version appears on this page with a new date. The full history is in the public repository.
privacy_contact_body: Questions about privacy: open an issue on GitHub. Security problems: report them privately through GitHub's vulnerability reporting.
